mvp_title: Farm to Table - Custom Livestock Cut Sheet Tool
summary: The cut-custom MVP is a card-based livestock selection interface designed for farm-to-table meat processing. The tool allows customers to select livestock types (beef, pork, lamb, goat) and customize their cut sheets. Research confirms 'Farm to Table' is a generic placeholder, not a specific business entity. Ashtabula County and Northeast Ohio have a robust ecosystem of meat processors, lockers, and farms that would benefit from digital cut sheet customization. The region has strong agricultural roots with both USDA-inspected facilities and custom exempt processors serving local farmers and consumers.

leads.name: Trumbull Locker Plant
leads.fit_rationale: Family-owned since 1947, offers complete meat processing with custom cut options. They have a fresh meat counter, deli, and produce section. Already serves the local farm community and processes beef, pork, and chicken. The custom cut sheet tool would streamline their customer ordering process and reduce manual paperwork.

leads.name: NaKyrsie Meats
leads.type: USDA Inspected Whole Animal Butcher Shop
leads.fit_rationale: USDA inspected whole animal butcher shop specializing in charcuterie and salumi. Ohio Proud member since 2019. Produces nitrate-free salamis, hams, and bacons. Already sells to fine dining establishments in Ashtabula Harbor. A digital cut sheet tool would help them manage custom orders from restaurants and retail customers more efficiently.

leads.name: Bonner Farms Beef & Market
leads.fit_rationale: 100% vertically integrated beef operation - they own every step from growing cattle feed to butchering and delivery. Featured by Ohio Farm Bureau for premium beef marketing. Their market has butchers on staff who discuss specific cuts with customers. A digital cut sheet platform would integrate perfectly with their direct-to-consumer sales model.

leads.name: Cherry Valley Slaughtering & Processing
leads.fit_rationale: Reputable custom slaughtering facility in Ashtabula County. Known for fair-priced, high-quality meats. Listed in Ashtabula County Local Food Guide. Specializes in custom processing for local farmers and hunters. Would benefit from digital cut sheet management to replace paper-based order tracking.

leads.name: Millgate Farm
leads.fit_rationale: Family farm since 1961 raising heritage Berkshire pigs and Maine Anjou cows on 200+ acres of pasture and woods. Focus on natural, responsibly raised meats. They already market directly to consumers and would benefit from a cut sheet customization tool for customers ordering quarter/half/whole animals.

branding_quality_assessment.visual_identity: The MVP uses a generic 'Farm to Table' header that lacks specific business identity. The orange accent color is appropriate for agricultural/food context but not unique.
branding_quality_assessment.content_quality: The card-based selection interface is clean but relies solely on icons. No imagery of actual products or farm environment.
branding_quality_assessment.trust_signals: Missing - no business address, phone number, certifications (USDA, Ohio Proud), or farm photos that would establish legitimacy.
branding_quality_assessment.differentiation: Low - the interface looks like a template that could be used by any meat processor without customization.

site_improvements.details: Replace generic 'Farm to Table' text with actual business name, logo, and farm imagery
Replace icons with high-quality photos of actual meat cuts, livestock, and farm operations
Include USDA certification badges, Ohio Proud membership, farm address, contact information, and customer testimonials
Show customers a visual preview of their selected cuts before finalizing order
Include information about different cuts, cooking recommendations, and portion sizing guides

strengths: Clean, centered layout with good whitespace
Card-based design is intuitive for livestock selection
Clear visual hierarchy from title to cards to actions
Orange accent color appropriate for food/agricultural context
weaknesses: No imagery creates abstract, unengaging experience
No visual feedback on card selection
aesthetics_and_layout_notes.white_label_observations: The layout is highly modular and could work for any livestock processor. The card system for beef/pork/lamb/goat is standard across the industry. Typography is system-default and easily replaced.

whitelabel_potential.reasoning: The underlying architecture (livestock selection cards → cut sheet configuration) is a universal pattern used by meat lockers nationwide. The generic 'Farm to Table' branding is already placeholder-level, making it easy to swap in specific business identities.
whitelabel_potential.deployment_considerations: Each deployment would need: business name/logo, contact information, specific livestock types offered, custom cut options per species, pricing structure, and pickup/delivery logistics.

regional_market_context.geographic_focus: Ashtabula County, Ohio and Northeast Ohio region
market_characteristics: Strong agricultural heritage with active livestock raising
Mix of USDA-inspected and custom-exempt processors
Active farmers market scene (Jefferson, Orwell, Ashtabula Harbor)
Support from Ohio State University Extension and Farm Bureau
regional_market_context.competitive_landscape: Multiple established processors (Trumbull Locker, NaKyrsie, Cherry Valley) serve the region, but most still use paper-based cut sheet systems. Digital transformation opportunity exists.
regional_market_context.regulatory_environment: Ohio Department of Agriculture Division of Meat Inspection oversees facilities. Custom exempt processors serve farm owners; USDA-inspected can sell retail across state lines.
